---
title: "Getting started"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(contoso)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

contoso gives you the same retail dataset in two ways: as tables bundled
with the package, and as larger cloud versions you query through 'DuckDB'.

## Bundled tables

Loading the package makes eight tables available: `sales`, `orders`,
`orderrows`, `customer`, `product`, `store`, `fx` and `calendar`. They need no
download or connection.

```{r}
#| label: bundled
library(contoso)

dplyr::glimpse(sales)
```

Join them on their `_key` columns:

```{r}
#| label: join
sales |>
  dplyr::left_join(store, by = "store_key") |>
  dplyr::summarise(net_revenue = sum(net_revenue), .by = country_name) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(net_revenue))
```

## Larger datasets in 'DuckDB'

`create_contoso_duckdb()` streams the Parquet files from cloud storage into an
in-memory 'DuckDB' database. Pick a size by the number of `sales` rows:

| `size`     | `sales` rows |
|------------|-------------:|
| `"small"`  | 7,794        |
| `"medium"` | 2,349,091    |
| `"large"`  | 23,719,935   |
| `"mega"`   | 237,245,485  |

`"small"` is the same data as the bundled tables. The other sizes cover a
different date range and a much larger customer catalogue.

```{r}
#| label: duckdb
#| eval: false
db <- create_contoso_duckdb(size = "medium")
```

The result is a list with one lazy table per dataset and the connection,
`db$con`. Write dplyr as usual; it runs in 'DuckDB' until you `collect()`:

```{r}
#| label: duckdb-query
#| eval: false
db$sales |>
  dplyr::summarise(net_revenue = sum(net_revenue), .by = currency_code) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

Use `launch_ui()` to browse every table in the 'DuckDB' UI, and disconnect
when you are done:

```{r}
#| label: duckdb-close
#| eval: false
launch_ui(db$con)

DBI::dbDisconnect(db$con, shutdown = TRUE)
```

## Data dictionary

Every table and column is described in a
[data-dict](https://data-dict.tidyverse.org/) file, with keys, joins and
the formulas behind each measure:

```{r}
#| label: dict
#| eval: false
system.file("extdata", "small", "data-dict.yaml", package = "contoso")
```

Use `"cloud"` in place of `"small"` for the dictionary of the larger sizes.
